EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Total, Slots, MaxEra

ASSUME Total \in Nat /\ Slots \in Nat /\ MaxEra \in Nat

VARIABLES cabinet, courier, stamp, given, era

vars == <<cabinet, courier, stamp, given, era>>

SlotIds == 1..Slots

CourierSum ==
  LET f[i \in 0..Slots] == IF i = 0 THEN 0 ELSE f[i-1] + courier[i]
  IN f[Slots]

TypeOK ==
  /\ cabinet \in 0..Total
  /\ given \in 0..Total
  /\ era \in 0..MaxEra
  /\ courier \in [SlotIds -> 0..Total]
  /\ stamp \in [SlotIds -> 0..MaxEra]

Conserved == cabinet + CourierSum + given = Total

Init ==
  /\ cabinet = Total
  /\ given = 0
  /\ era = 0
  /\ courier = [i \in SlotIds |-> 0]
  /\ stamp = [i \in SlotIds |-> 0]

Load(m) ==
  /\ cabinet > 0
  /\ courier[m] = 0
  /\ cabinet' = cabinet - 1
  /\ courier' = [courier EXCEPT ![m] = 1]
  /\ stamp' = [stamp EXCEPT ![m] = era]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<given, era>>

Dispense(m) ==
  /\ courier[m] > 0
  /\ given' = given + courier[m]
  /\ courier' = [courier EXCEPT ![m] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cabinet, stamp, era>>

Reconfigure ==
  /\ era' = IF era < MaxEra THEN era + 1 ELSE 0
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cabinet, courier, stamp, given>>

Recall(m) ==
  /\ courier[m] > 0
  /\ stamp[m] < era
  /\ cabinet' = cabinet + courier[m]
  /\ courier' = [courier EXCEPT ![m] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<given, stamp, era>>

Next ==
  \/ \E m \in SlotIds : Load(m)
  \/ \E m \in SlotIds : Dispense(m)
  \/ \E m \in SlotIds : Recall(m)
  \/ Reconfigure

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CONSTANTS
    Total = 3
    Slots = 2
    MaxEra = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT Conserved
nl:
A hospital pharmacy runs an automated pill dispenser. All doses live in one of three places: the central cabinet, a courier bag on its way to a ward, or already given to a patient. Because the total number of doses in the building must never change on its own, the system tracks conservation across every location.

The dispenser reconfigures itself in numbered eras: each reconfiguration bumps the current era number so that older courier bags can be recognized as stale.

The actions are:
- Load: take one dose out of the central cabinet and place it into an empty courier bag, stamping the bag with the current era number.
- Dispense: take a courier bag that holds doses and record all of them as given to a patient, emptying the bag. Bags may be dispensed in any order, not necessarily the order they were loaded.
- Reconfigure: advance the era number by one; once it reaches the fixed maximum the next reconfiguration wraps it back to zero, so a reconfiguration is always available.
- Recall: take a courier bag whose stamp is older than the current era (a stale, reordered message) and return its doses to the central cabinet, emptying the bag.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of doses in the cabinet plus those in all courier bags plus those already given to patients always equals the fixed total, so no dose is ever created or destroyed.

CONSTANTS
    Titles = {t1, t2}
    LeaseLen = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoDoubleLease
nl:
A city library reservation service runs two independent branch instances, North and South, that both draw from a single shared pool of book copies. When a branch grants a reservation it takes a lease on that copy, and the lease has a fixed lifetime measured in shared pool ticks. When the lease runs out the copy returns to the pool automatically.

The actions are:
- RequestNorth: the North branch records that a patron wants a particular copy (raises its want flag for that copy).
- RequestSouth: the South branch records that a patron wants a particular copy.
- GrantNorth: if North has a pending want for a copy that is currently held by neither branch, North takes a lease on it for the full lease lifetime and clears its want flag.
- GrantSouth: symmetrically, South takes a lease on a copy held by neither branch.
- PoolClock: one shared pool tick advances the beat and decrements every active lease's remaining lifetime by one, freeing any lease that reaches zero.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No single copy is ever simultaneously under an active lease held by both the North and the South branch.

CONSTANTS
    Branches = {east, west}
    nil = nil
    MaxEpoch = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT Authorized
nl:
A regional library reservation system serves two independent branch instances, east and west, that share a single pool of shelves and books. Access is protected by a two-level hierarchical lock: a branch must first take the coarse lock on a shelf, and only then may it take a fine lock on an individual book sitting on that shelf. The whole pool is versioned by a configuration epoch; a reconfiguration bumps the epoch and wipes every lock, which leaves any branch whose session was validated under the old epoch stale.

The actions are:
- GrabShelf: a branch takes the coarse lock on a free shelf, and in doing so its session is validated at the current configuration epoch.
- GrabBook: a branch takes the fine lock on a free book, but only if it already holds the coarse lock on that book's shelf and its session is validated at the current epoch.
- DropBook: a branch releases a fine lock it holds on a book.
- DropShelf: a branch releases the coarse lock on a shelf, permitted only once it holds no fine lock on any book of that shelf.
- Reconfigure: the pool advances its configuration epoch (wrapping to zero past a maximum) and releases every coarse and fine lock, leaving old sessions stale.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a book's fine lock is held, the holder also holds the coarse lock on that book's shelf and its session is validated at the current epoch, so no unauthorized or stale branch ever holds a book.

ASSUME MinCap \in Nat /\ MaxCap \in Nat /\ MinCap <= MaxCap

VARIABLES journal, readLen, acked, blockCap, midWrite

vars == <<journal, readLen, acked, blockCap, midWrite>>

Range(s) == { s[i] : i \in 1..Len(s) }

TypeOK ==
  /\ journal \in Seq(Interlockings)
  /\ readLen \in [Interlockings -> 0..MaxCap]
  /\ acked \subseteq Interlockings
  /\ blockCap \in MinCap..MaxCap
  /\ midWrite \in [Interlockings -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
  /\ journal = << >>
  /\ readLen = [k \in Interlockings |-> 0]
  /\ acked = {}
  /\ blockCap = MinCap
  /\ midWrite = [k \in Interlockings |-> FALSE]

NoLostUpdate == acked \subseteq Range(journal)

Snapshot(k) ==
  /\ ~midWrite[k]
  /\ readLen' = [readLen EXCEPT ![k] = Len(journal)]
  /\ midWrite' = [midWrite EXCEPT ![k] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<journal, acked, blockCap>>

CommitCAS(k) ==
  /\ midWrite[k]
  /\ readLen[k] = Len(journal)
  /\ Len(journal) < blockCap
  /\ k \notin acked
  /\ journal' = Append(journal, k)
  /\ acked' = acked \cup {k}
  /\ midWrite' = [midWrite EXCEPT ![k] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<readLen, blockCap>>

Retry(k) ==
  /\ midWrite[k]
  /\ readLen[k] # Len(journal)
  /\ readLen' = [readLen EXCEPT ![k] = Len(journal)]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<journal, acked, blockCap, midWrite>>

AdjustCapacity ==
  /\ blockCap' = IF blockCap = MaxCap THEN MinCap ELSE blockCap + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<journal, readLen, acked, midWrite>>

Next ==
  \/ \E k \in Interlockings : Snapshot(k)
  \/ \E k \in Interlockings : CommitCAS(k)
  \/ \E k \in Interlockings : Retry(k)
  \/ AdjustCapacity

CONSTANTS
    Interlockings = {ilA, ilB}
    MaxCap = 2
    MinCap = 1
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
A subway signalling block system keeps one shared movement journal that interlocking controllers append to. Because several controllers race to record train movements into the same block record, each write is guarded by a compare-and-swap on the journal's length: a controller may only append if the journal is still exactly as long as it was when the controller last read it. The block's capacity is not fixed; it is retuned at runtime as track conditions change.

The actions are:
- Snapshot: a controller reads the current journal length and enters a mid-write state, remembering that length as its expected value.
- CommitCAS: a controller in mid-write whose remembered length still equals the current journal length, while the journal is below capacity and the controller has not already been acknowledged, appends its own movement token to the journal and is marked acknowledged.
- Retry: a controller in mid-write whose remembered length no longer matches the current journal length (another controller appended first) re-reads the current length instead of writing.
- AdjustCapacity: the block capacity is retuned at runtime, cycling upward through the allowed range and wrapping back to the minimum past the maximum.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every controller that has been acknowledged as having committed still has its movement token present in the shared journal, so no committed update is ever lost.

--------------------- MODULE W4Od12m7p3t3 ---------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Units, Hospitals, free, noU

ASSUME free \notin Hospitals /\ noU \notin Units

VARIABLES slotReg, holds, phase, target, tempo

vars == <<slotReg, holds, phase, target, tempo>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ slotReg \in [Units -> Hospitals \cup {free}]
  /\ holds \in [Hospitals -> SUBSET Units]
  /\ phase \in [Hospitals -> {"idle", "claimed", "settling", "done"}]
  /\ target \in [Hospitals -> Units \cup {noU}]
  /\ tempo \in [Hospitals -> {"quick", "slow"}]

Init ==
  /\ slotReg = [u \in Units |-> free]
  /\ holds = [h \in Hospitals |-> {}]
  /\ phase = [h \in Hospitals |-> "idle"]
  /\ target = [h \in Hospitals |-> noU]
  /\ tempo = [h \in Hospitals |-> "quick"]

NoDoubleAlloc ==
  \A h1 \in Hospitals, h2 \in Hospitals :
     h1 # h2 => (holds[h1] \cap holds[h2] = {})

ClaimCAS(h, u) ==
  /\ phase[h] = "idle"
  /\ slotReg[u] = free
  /\ slotReg' = [slotReg EXCEPT ![u] = h]
  /\ target' = [target EXCEPT ![h] = u]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![h] = "claimed"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holds, tempo>>

FinalizeQuick(h) ==
  /\ phase[h] = "claimed"
  /\ tempo[h] = "quick"
  /\ holds' = [holds EXCEPT ![h] = holds[h] \cup {target[h]}]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![h] = "done"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<slotReg, target, tempo>>

SlowSettle(h) ==
  /\ phase[h] = "claimed"
  /\ tempo[h] = "slow"
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![h] = "settling"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<slotReg, holds, target, tempo>>

FinalizeSlow(h) ==
  /\ phase[h] = "settling"
  /\ holds' = [holds EXCEPT ![h] = holds[h] \cup {target[h]}]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![h] = "done"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<slotReg, target, tempo>>

ReleaseSlot(h) ==
  /\ phase[h] = "done"
  /\ slotReg' = [slotReg EXCEPT ![target[h]] = free]
  /\ holds' = [holds EXCEPT ![h] = holds[h] \ {target[h]}]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![h] = "idle"]
  /\ target' = [target EXCEPT ![h] = noU]
  /\ UNCHANGED tempo

FlipTempo(h) ==
  /\ tempo' = [tempo EXCEPT ![h] = IF tempo[h] = "quick" THEN "slow" ELSE "quick"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<slotReg, holds, phase, target>>

Next ==
  \/ \E h \in Hospitals, u \in Units : ClaimCAS(h, u)
  \/ \E h \in Hospitals : FinalizeQuick(h)
  \/ \E h \in Hospitals : SlowSettle(h)
  \/ \E h \in Hospitals : FinalizeSlow(h)
  \/ \E h \in Hospitals : ReleaseSlot(h)
  \/ \E h \in Hospitals : FlipTempo(h)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Units = {u1, u2}
    Hospitals = {ha, hb}
    free = free
    noU = noU
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoDoubleAlloc
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker hands out individual blood units to hospitals. Each unit has a single compare-and-swap ownership register that starts free. A hospital claims a unit only by swapping that register from free to itself. Hospitals may be slow but never fail: a slow hospital takes an extra settling step before it finalizes, but it always eventually finalizes and never drops a unit it has claimed.

The actions are:
- ClaimCAS: an idle hospital atomically swaps a free unit's register to itself, records the unit as its target, and moves into the claimed phase.
- FinalizeQuick: a quick-tempo hospital in the claimed phase records the target unit into its own holdings and becomes done.
- SlowSettle: a slow-tempo hospital in the claimed phase takes an intermediate settling step, keeping its register reservation while it lingers.
- FinalizeSlow: a hospital in the settling phase records the target unit into its holdings and becomes done.
- ReleaseSlot: a done hospital frees the unit's register, removes the unit from its holdings, clears its target, and returns to idle.
- FlipTempo: a hospital toggles between quick and slow tempo.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No blood unit is ever simultaneously present in the holdings of two different hospitals.

  /\ hoistTok \in Cars \cup {none}
  /\ mode \in [Cars -> {"parked", "zoned", "riding"}]
  /\ callPool \subseteq Cars
  /\ dispatchedBy \in [Cars -> Controllers \cup {unassigned}]

  /\ dispatchedBy[c] = unassigned

  /\ hoistTok' = c

  /\ hoistTok' = none
  /\ zoneTok' = none
  /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![c] = "parked"]
  /\ dispatchedBy' = [dispatchedBy EXCEPT ![c] = unassigned]
  /\ UNCHANGED callPool

  \/ \E g \in Controllers, c \in Cars : Dispatch(g, c)

CONSTANTS
    Cars = {c1, c2}
    Controllers = {ctrlA, ctrlB}
    none = none
    unassigned = unassigned
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT MutualExclusion
nl:
A skyscraper elevator bank has several cars but only one critical hoistway that a car must own to ride. Two independent dispatch controllers share a single pool of hall calls. Access is guarded by hierarchical locks: a car must first take the coarse zone token, and only while holding it may it take the fine hoist token that lets it ride.

The actions are:
- HallCall: an idle, unassigned, parked car registers a hall call into the shared call pool.
- Dispatch: either controller picks an unassigned call from the shared pool and assigns that car to itself, removing the call from the pool.
- GrabZone: a parked car that has been dispatched takes the coarse zone token if it is free, moving into the zoned state.
- GrabHoist: a zoned car that holds the zone token takes the free fine hoist token and begins riding.
- Exit: a riding car releases both the hoist token and the zone token, returns to parked, and becomes unassigned again.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any car that is riding holds the single hoist token, which therefore lets at most one car ride the critical hoistway at a time (mutual exclusion of the hoist).

--------------------- MODULE W4Od15m0p0t0 ---------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Traders, none, MaxVer

ASSUME none \notin Traders /\ MaxVer \in Nat

VARIABLES lock, ver, view, phase, crashed

vars == <<lock, ver, view, phase, crashed>>

Bump(v) == IF v < MaxVer THEN v + 1 ELSE 0

TypeOK ==
  /\ lock \in Traders \cup {none}
  /\ ver \in 0..MaxVer
  /\ view \in [Traders -> 0..MaxVer]
  /\ phase \in [Traders -> {"idle", "trying", "inside", "gone"}]
  /\ crashed \subseteq Traders

Init ==
  /\ lock = none
  /\ ver = 0
  /\ view = [t \in Traders |-> 0]
  /\ phase = [t \in Traders |-> "idle"]
  /\ crashed = {}

MutualExclusion ==
  \A t \in Traders : phase[t] = "inside" => lock = t

ReadVer(t) ==
  /\ phase[t] = "idle"
  /\ t \notin crashed
  /\ view' = [view EXCEPT ![t] = ver]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "trying"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lock, ver, crashed>>

AttemptEnter(t) ==
  /\ phase[t] = "trying"
  /\ view[t] = ver
  /\ lock = none
  /\ lock' = t
  /\ ver' = Bump(ver)
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "inside"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<view, crashed>>

RetryRead(t) ==
  /\ phase[t] = "trying"
  /\ view[t] # ver
  /\ view' = [view EXCEPT ![t] = ver]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lock, ver, phase, crashed>>

Leave(t) ==
  /\ phase[t] = "inside"
  /\ lock' = none
  /\ ver' = Bump(ver)
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<view, crashed>>

CrashSilently(t) ==
  /\ crashed = {}
  /\ t \notin crashed
  /\ crashed' = {t}
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "gone"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lock, ver, view>>

Reclaim(t) ==
  /\ t \in crashed
  /\ lock = t
  /\ lock' = none
  /\ ver' = Bump(ver)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<view, phase, crashed>>

Next ==
  \/ \E t \in Traders : ReadVer(t)
  \/ \E t \in Traders : AttemptEnter(t)
  \/ \E t \in Traders : RetryRead(t)
  \/ \E t \in Traders : Leave(t)
  \/ \E t \in Traders : CrashSilently(t)
  \/ \E t \in Traders : Reclaim(t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

===============================================================

CONSTANTS
    Traders = {ta, tb}
    none = none
    MaxVer = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT MutualExclusion
nl:
A stock exchange runs an opening auction whose price-fixing engine is a single critical section only one trader may occupy at a time. Traders use optimistic locking: a trader reads the engine's version counter, then tries to enter, and only succeeds if the version has not changed since the read; otherwise it re-reads and retries. One trader may crash silently at any moment and stop participating; a watchdog reclaims the lock if a crashed trader was holding it.

The actions are:
- ReadVer: an idle, live trader reads the current version counter and moves into the trying state.
- AttemptEnter: a trying trader whose remembered version still equals the current version, and only when the lock is free, takes the lock, bumps the version, and enters the critical section.
- RetryRead: a trying trader whose remembered version no longer matches the current version re-reads the current version.
- Leave: a trader inside the critical section releases the lock, bumps the version, and returns to idle.
- CrashSilently: at most one trader ever crashes; it stops acting and enters the gone state.
- Reclaim: the watchdog frees the lock and bumps the version when the lock is held by the crashed trader.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any trader inside the critical section holds the lock, so at most one trader is ever inside the price-fixing engine at once.

Leadership uses failover: a node is elected when there is no leader and can step down so another takes over. Requester nodes ask the leader for units, and the leader grants only within the pool capacity. One node may crash silently; its allocation still counts against capacity until it is reclaimed, and if the leader itself crashes the network is left leaderless.

The actions are:
- Elect: when there is no leader, a live node becomes leader in a bumped term.
- StepDown: the current leader steps down, leaving the network leaderless.
- Request: a node with no pending request asks for a number of units.
- Grant: the leader satisfies a node's pending request, but only if the running allocation total plus the request stays within capacity.
- CrashSilently: at most one node crashes silently; if it was the leader, leadership is cleared, while its allocation remains held.
- Reclaim: a crashed node's held allocation is returned to the pool.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The total units allocated across all nodes never exceeds the pool capacity (this bounded-capacity bound is exactly the property).

--------------------- MODULE W4Od4m4p5t1 ---------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Cars, Cap, none

ASSUME Cap \in Nat /\ none \notin Cars

VARIABLES waiting, lineup, onWax, waxed, ready, beat

vars == <<waiting, lineup, onWax, waxed, ready, beat>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ waiting \subseteq Cars
  /\ lineup \subseteq Cars
  /\ onWax \in Cars \cup {none}
  /\ waxed \subseteq Cars
  /\ ready \subseteq Cars
  /\ beat \in {0, 1}

Init ==
  /\ waiting = Cars
  /\ lineup = {}
  /\ onWax = none
  /\ waxed = {}
  /\ ready = {}
  /\ beat = 0

AtMostOnce ==
  \A c \in Cars :
     c \in waxed => (c \notin lineup /\ c \notin waiting /\ onWax # c)

Enter(c) ==
  /\ c \in waiting
  /\ c \notin waxed
  /\ Cardinality(lineup) < Cap
  /\ lineup' = lineup \cup {c}
  /\ waiting' = waiting \ {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<onWax, waxed, ready, beat>>

Ready(c) ==
  /\ c \in lineup
  /\ c \notin ready
  /\ ready' = ready \cup {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, lineup, onWax, waxed, beat>>

StartWax(c) ==
  /\ onWax = none
  /\ c \in ready
  /\ c \in lineup
  /\ c \notin waxed
  /\ onWax' = c
  /\ lineup' = lineup \ {c}
  /\ ready' = ready \ {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, waxed, beat>>

FinishWax ==
  /\ onWax # none
  /\ onWax \notin waxed
  /\ waxed' = waxed \cup {onWax}
  /\ onWax' = none
  /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, lineup, ready, beat>>

Heartbeat ==
  /\ beat' = 1 - beat
  /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, lineup, onWax, waxed, ready>>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Cars : Enter(c)
  \/ \E c \in Cars : Ready(c)
  \/ \E c \in Cars : StartWax(c)
  \/ FinishWax
  \/ Heartbeat

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

===============================================================

CONSTANTS
    Cars = {c1, c2}
    Cap = 2
    none = none
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT AtMostOnce
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line pulls cars through a bounded lineup with backpressure: a car may only join the lineup while it is below its capacity. The wax coat is irreversible, so each car must be waxed at most once. Cars signal that they are ready for wax, and those ready signals may be consumed in any order, so the wax station does not pull strictly in lineup order.

The actions are:
- Enter: a waiting, not-yet-waxed car joins the lineup, allowed only while the lineup is below capacity.
- Ready: a car in the lineup emits a ready-for-wax signal.
- StartWax: when the wax station is free, it pulls any car that has signalled ready and is still in the lineup and not yet waxed, removing it from the lineup (regardless of position).
- FinishWax: the car at the wax station receives its irreversible wax coat and is recorded as waxed, freeing the station.
- Heartbeat: the conveyor belt keeps running, toggling its power beat.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any car that has been waxed is no longer waiting, in the lineup, or at the wax station, so no car is ever waxed a second time.

--------------------- MODULE W4Od19m3p2t5 ---------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Nodes, none, Total, MaxTerm

ASSUME Total \in Nat /\ MaxTerm \in Nat /\ none \notin Nodes

VARIABLES leader, term, onShelf, onLoan, reserved, adminArmed

vars == <<leader, term, onShelf, onLoan, reserved, adminArmed>>

Bump(t) == IF t < MaxTerm THEN t + 1 ELSE 0

TypeOK ==
  /\ leader \in Nodes \cup {none}
  /\ term \in 0..MaxTerm
  /\ onShelf \in 0..Total
  /\ onLoan \in 0..Total
  /\ reserved \in 0..Total
  /\ adminArmed \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
  /\ leader = none
  /\ term = 0
  /\ onShelf = Total
  /\ onLoan = 0
  /\ reserved = 0
  /\ adminArmed = FALSE

Conserved == onShelf + onLoan + reserved = Total

Elect(n) ==
  /\ leader = none
  /\ leader' = n
  /\ term' = Bump(term)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<onShelf, onLoan, reserved, adminArmed>>

StepDown(n) ==
  /\ leader = n
  /\ leader' = none
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, onShelf, onLoan, reserved, adminArmed>>

Reserve ==
  /\ leader # none
  /\ onShelf > 0
  /\ onShelf' = onShelf - 1
  /\ reserved' = reserved + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, onLoan, adminArmed>>

Lend ==
  /\ leader # none
  /\ reserved > 0
  /\ reserved' = reserved - 1
  /\ onLoan' = onLoan + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, onShelf, adminArmed>>

Return ==
  /\ onLoan > 0
  /\ onLoan' = onLoan - 1
  /\ onShelf' = onShelf + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, reserved, adminArmed>>

AdminForceReturn ==
  /\ adminArmed
  /\ reserved > 0
  /\ reserved' = reserved - 1
  /\ onShelf' = onShelf + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, onLoan, adminArmed>>

ToggleAdmin ==
  /\ adminArmed' = ~adminArmed
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, onShelf, onLoan, reserved>>

Next ==
  \/ \E n \in Nodes : Elect(n)
  \/ \E n \in Nodes : StepDown(n)
  \/ Reserve
  \/ Lend
  \/ Return
  \/ AdminForceReturn
  \/ ToggleAdmin

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

    Nodes = {n1, n2}
    none = none
    Total = 3
    MaxTerm = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT Conserved
nl:
A library book reservation system tracks a fixed number of copies of a title, coordinated by an elected leader node. Every copy is always in exactly one place: on the shelf, out on loan, or reserved and in transit between the two. Leadership uses failover: a node is elected when there is no leader and can step down so another takes over. A privileged admin can force a stuck reservation back to the shelf.

The actions are:
- Elect: when there is no leader, a node becomes leader in a bumped term.
- StepDown: the current leader steps down, leaving the system leaderless.
- Reserve: the leader moves one copy from the shelf into the reserved-in-transit state.
- Lend: the leader turns one reserved copy into a copy out on loan.
- Return: a patron returns one on-loan copy to the shelf.
- AdminForceReturn: while the admin override is armed, the admin cancels one reserved copy and puts it directly back on the shelf.
- ToggleAdmin: the admin override is armed or disarmed.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of copies on the shelf, out on loan, and reserved always sums to the fixed total, so no copy is ever created or destroyed.

--------------------- MODULE W4Od13m7p4t5 ---------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Machines, Cap, MaxGen

ASSUME Cap \in Nat /\ MaxGen \in Nat

VARIABLES stock, inTray, stockGen, snap, adminArmed

vars == <<stock, inTray, stockGen, snap, adminArmed>>

Bump(g) == IF g < MaxGen THEN g + 1 ELSE 0

TypeOK ==
  /\ stock \in 0..Cap
  /\ inTray \in 0..Cap
  /\ stockGen \in 0..MaxGen
  /\ snap \in [Machines -> 0..MaxGen]
  /\ adminArmed \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
  /\ stock = 0
  /\ inTray = 0
  /\ stockGen = 0
  /\ snap = [m \in Machines |-> 0]
  /\ adminArmed = FALSE

WithinCapacity == stock + inTray <= Cap

ReadStock(m) ==
  /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![m] = stockGen]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, inTray, stockGen, adminArmed>>

RefillCAS(m) ==
  /\ snap[m] = stockGen
  /\ stock + inTray < Cap
  /\ stock' = stock + 1
  /\ stockGen' = Bump(stockGen)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<inTray, snap, adminArmed>>

RefillRetry(m) ==
  /\ snap[m] # stockGen
  /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![m] = stockGen]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, inTray, stockGen, adminArmed>>

Dispense ==
  /\ stock > 0
  /\ stock' = stock - 1
  /\ inTray' = inTray + 1
  /\ stockGen' = Bump(stockGen)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, adminArmed>>

Collect ==
  /\ inTray > 0
  /\ inTray' = inTray - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, stockGen, snap, adminArmed>>

AdminTopUp(m) ==
  /\ adminArmed
  /\ stock + inTray < Cap
  /\ stock' = stock + 1
  /\ stockGen' = Bump(stockGen)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<inTray, snap, adminArmed>>

ToggleAdmin ==
  /\ adminArmed' = ~adminArmed
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, inTray, stockGen, snap>>

Next ==
  \/ \E m \in Machines : ReadStock(m)
  \/ \E m \in Machines : RefillCAS(m)
  \/ \E m \in Machines : RefillRetry(m)
  \/ Dispense
  \/ Collect
  \/ \E m \in Machines : AdminTopUp(m)
  \/ ToggleAdmin

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CONSTANTS
    Machines = {mA, mB}
    Cap = 2
    MaxGen = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT WithinCapacity
nl:
A network of vending machines shares one inventory register guarded by compare-and-swap. Each physical unit is either in stock or sitting in the dispense tray waiting to be collected, and the machine's total physical contents must never exceed its capacity. Restock writers use CAS against a stock generation counter so concurrent refills cannot overshoot capacity. A privileged operator admin can top up directly.

The actions are:
- ReadStock: a machine reads the current stock generation into its snapshot for a later compare-and-swap.
- RefillCAS: a machine whose snapshot still matches the stock generation adds one unit to stock and bumps the generation, but only while stock plus tray contents are below capacity.
- RefillRetry: a machine whose snapshot no longer matches the stock generation refreshes its snapshot.
- Dispense: one unit moves from stock into the dispense tray and the generation is bumped.
- Collect: a customer removes one unit from the dispense tray.
- AdminTopUp: while the admin override is armed, the operator adds one unit to stock directly, bypassing the CAS but still only while below capacity.
- ToggleAdmin: the admin override is armed or disarmed.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of units in stock plus those in the dispense tray never exceeds the machine's capacity (this bounded-capacity bound is exactly the property).

--------------------- MODULE W4Od8m7p3t2 ---------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Seats, Students, Portals, open, noSeat

ASSUME open \notin Students /\ noSeat \notin Seats

VARIABLES seatReg, seatOf, portal, stage

vars == <<seatReg, seatOf, portal, stage>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ seatReg \in [Seats -> Students \cup {open}]
  /\ seatOf \in [Students -> Seats \cup {noSeat}]
  /\ portal \in [Students -> Portals]
  /\ stage \in [Students -> {"browse", "trying", "seated"}]

Init ==
  /\ seatReg = [s \in Seats |-> open]
  /\ seatOf = [st \in Students |-> noSeat]
  /\ portal = [st \in Students |-> CHOOSE i \in Portals : TRUE]
  /\ stage = [st \in Students |-> "browse"]

NoDoubleAlloc ==
  \A a \in Students, b \in Students :
     (a # b /\ stage[a] = "seated" /\ stage[b] = "seated")
        => seatOf[a] # seatOf[b]

Route(st, inst) ==
  /\ stage[st] = "browse"
  /\ portal[st] # inst
  /\ portal' = [portal EXCEPT ![st] = inst]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<seatReg, seatOf, stage>>

Attempt(st, s) ==
  /\ stage[st] = "browse"
  /\ seatOf' = [seatOf EXCEPT ![st] = s]
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![st] = "trying"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<seatReg, portal>>

ClaimCAS(st) ==
  /\ stage[st] = "trying"
  /\ seatReg[seatOf[st]] = open
  /\ seatReg' = [seatReg EXCEPT ![seatOf[st]] = st]
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![st] = "seated"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<seatOf, portal>>

Backoff(st) ==
  /\ stage[st] = "trying"
  /\ seatReg[seatOf[st]] # open
  /\ seatOf' = [seatOf EXCEPT ![st] = noSeat]
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![st] = "browse"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<seatReg, portal>>

Release(st) ==
  /\ stage[st] = "seated"
  /\ seatReg' = [seatReg EXCEPT ![seatOf[st]] = open]
  /\ seatOf' = [seatOf EXCEPT ![st] = noSeat]
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![st] = "browse"]
  /\ UNCHANGED portal

Next ==
  \/ \E st \in Students, inst \in Portals : Route(st, inst)
  \/ \E st \in Students, s \in Seats : Attempt(st, s)
  \/ \E st \in Students : ClaimCAS(st)
  \/ \E st \in Students : Backoff(st)
  \/ \E st \in Students : Release(st)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

===============================================================
nl:
A university course-registration system exposes two independent registration portals that share one pool of seats. Each seat has an ownership register that starts open. A student claims a seat by compare-and-swap, swapping the register from open to itself; if the register is no longer open (the other portal's student grabbed it first) the student backs off and retries.

The actions are:
- Route: a browsing student is handed to a different one of the two independent portals.
- Attempt: a browsing student targets a seat and moves into the trying state.
- ClaimCAS: a trying student whose targeted seat register is still open atomically swaps it to itself and becomes seated.
- Backoff: a trying student whose targeted seat register is no longer open clears its target and returns to browsing.
- Release: a seated student vacates its seat, marking the register open again and returning to browsing.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No two distinct seated students ever hold the same seat.
